reviewer.actual_effort: Final adjudication, not a new blind reading. I read all of current.json, current-xml.xml, page-audits.json, guideline-excerpts.md, english-rest-resolutions.json and both full source-review reports (s118-125, s126-133). I compared the English text word for word and mark by mark against the full original images s123, s125, s127 and s129 at the displayed resolution, about 1208x2000 from a 1368x2264 original. I made no enlarged crops because no English reading was ambiguous. I opened the Hebrew page s126 only to check the shared conditional boundary and rubric placement for Naalah. I did not proofread any Hebrew.

scope: English source accuracy, its encoding against the guideline excerpts, and the shared English/Hebrew correspondence, condition and alignment boundaries for 8 witnesses: shacharit_elohai_netzor, shacharit_yehi_ratzon_temple, repetition_avot_open, misod_chakhamim, et_chil_yom_pequddah, naalah_vedin, taalat_zo, melekh_bedin. Hebrew transcription and fine marks are excluded.

issues.problem: title.en is the Hebrew string 'ברכת אבות — פתיחה', not an English title. It is not emitted into the English XML body and is not source text.
issues.fix: Optional: give it an English label, or leave it if Hebrew title fallback is the project convention.

issues.location: English XML: </tei:p> after 'Central between past and future' and the new <tei:p> before 'was he hewn' (s125→s127). The Hebrew project has the same pattern.
issues.problem: The printed English paragraph runs on across the page turn: s127 opens 'was he hewn' with no indent. The encoding starts a new tei:p there, which suggests a paragraph break the source does not print. The guideline asks for printed p structure to be kept apart from reference boundaries. The part_1/part_2 boundary is the same on both sides, so alignment is not affected.
issues.fix: Optional: keep one tei:p with the pb and part_2 milestone inside it, as elohai_netzor already does at its page break. If the split is a deliberate project convention for divisions at a page turn, leave it.

issues.severity: medium (blocking for exact English source fidelity)
issues.location: English XML j:conditional xml:id=naalah_vedin_segment_2, child <tei:note type="instruction" xml:lang="en">On Sabbath:</tei:note>; current.json condition_instruction 'On Sabbath:'
issues.problem: The English page prints no Sabbath rubric. s127, Naalah paragraph lines 2–3, reads exactly 'But with the Shofar (the memory of the Shofar) I appease Him'. The only printed rubric is the Hebrew 'אם שבת' inside the parenthesis on s126, line 2 of the stanza: '(אם שבת בזכרון שופר)'. The English witness therefore carries a rubric with no printed source, and it would be printed whenever the condition is undefined. The guideline makes the instruction of a type="marked" scope optional ('with its instruction, if it has one'), so the parentheses alone are a complete encoding.
issues.fix: Remove the English tei:note and keep j:conditional type="marked" with only the fs. Alternatively, if supplying English rubrics is a documented project policy, give the note a shared instruction corresp with the Hebrew 'אם שבת' and record it as editorial so it is not treated as printed source. Leave the running text, the condition extents (the Shofar / the memory of the Shofar) and the features as they are.

issues.location: English XML whitespace around segment_1 and segment_2
issues.problem: There is a double space before the first conditional, and a trailing space inside each conditional before j:endConditional. When the condition is undefined and brackets are added, this may produce '[the memory of the Shofar ]'.
issues.fix: Optional: move the trailing spaces outside the endConditional markers. This is a markup tidy-up, not a source error.

issues.severity: medium (blocking for exact English source fidelity)
issues.location: English XML j:conditional xml:id=melekh_bedin_segment_2, child <tei:note type="instruction" xml:lang="en">On Sabbath:</tei:note>; current.json condition_instruction 'On Sabbath:'
issues.problem: This is the same defect as naalah_vedin. s129, Melekh paragraph lines 2–3, prints 'but with the Shofar (the memory of the Shofar) I appease Him' with no English Sabbath rubric. The encoded English rubric is not in the English source.
issues.fix: Same fix as naalah_vedin: remove the English note and keep the marked conditional, or give it a shared corresp with the Hebrew rubric and record it as editorial.

issues.location: English XML whitespace around segment_1 and segment_2
issues.problem: Same double and trailing spaces as naalah_vedin, with the same possible '[the memory of the Shofar ]'.
issues.fix: Optional: move the spaces outside the conditionals.

verified: s123 (English p. 47), Elohai Netzor opening: matches the image word for word and in punctuation through 'devise evil against'. The page-audits file has no s123 entry, because the s118-125 report reviewed s118, s120, s122, s124 and s125 only. This page is certified by my own direct image comparison in this review.

s125 (English p. 48): Elohai Netzor continuation, Yehi Ratzon with Malachi 3:4, Barukh (including the curly ’ in children’s and Name’s), Misod, and Et chil through 'Central between past and future' all match. The faint 'pleasaŭt' in Yehi Ratzon is print damage to 'pleasant', not a typo. This agrees with the s118-125 report's s125 finding.

s127 (English p. 49): Et chil continuation through 'with which she had been considered.' and the Naalah running text match exactly, including the commas in 'with bent knee, in the shelter of friends,' and '(the Sanctuary)'. This agrees with the s126-133 report's s127 finding of no discrepancies.

s129 (English p. 50): the Taalat zo and Melekh running text match exactly, including '(Hannah)', '(Abraham)', '(Isaac)', 'primaeval', 'acknowledgment', and 'with bent knee in the dew of revival' with no comma. This agrees with the s126-133 report's s129 finding.
Ledger: english-rest-resolutions.json has no corrections for these 8 witnesses, and current original_source_typo_corrections is empty for them. No duplicate or outstanding English correction applies.
The Hebrew incipit cues printed before the English paragraphs (אלהי, יהי, ברוך, מסוד, את חיל, נעלה, תאלת, מלך) are correctly left out, as the scope rules require.

Shared correspondence: in every pair, the English and Hebrew prayer-part milestones (open and terminator), the div corresp and the pb page numbers 47–50 match. The Et chil part_1/part_2 boundary matches in meaning ('future | was he hewn' = 'כְּתָוֶךְ | נֶחְצַב').

Scripture: Psalms 60:7, Psalms 19:15 and Malachi 3:4 have the same verse extents on both sides ('so that those who love Thee…respond to me' = 'לְמַעַן יֵחָלְצוּן…וַעֲנֵנִי'). Each sits in a bounded seg with a canonical source, under local chapter/verse milestones with bare terminators, following the established occurrence-context convention.

Naalah and Melekh conditions: the English and Hebrew extents line up ('the Shofar' = 'בְּשׁוֹפָר'; 'the memory of the Shofar' = 'בְּזִכְרוֹן שׁוֹפָר'). The holiday-aggregate shabbat false/true pair is correct. type="marked" correctly stands for the printed parentheses, which are not encoded as literal text. s126 confirms that the Hebrew rubric אם שבת is printed inside the parenthesis, so the Hebrew-side condition rubric has a printed source.
Misod, Et chil, Naalah, Taalat and Melekh: the standoff variant notes are Hebrew-only and have no English anchors, which is correct because the English prints no variants.
limits: This is not a Hebrew approval. Hebrew readings, sigla, anchor placement and fine marks flagged in the s124, s126 and s128 reports (for example the Et chil and Taalat zo consonantal misreadings, the ק׳ sigla, and the variant anchor positions) remain pending and were not adjudicated. I viewed s126 only to locate the Sabbath rubric.
There is no audit-report coverage of s123 in page-audits.json or in the s118-125 full report. Approval of the Elohai Netzor opening rests on my own direct comparison with the original s123 image.
I did not check renderer output, exporter settings or the effect of whitespace normalization. The whitespace notes are markup observations only.

I did not check repository tests, refdb UNIT_CONTAINED_BY or any project policy on editorially supplied English rubrics. If such a policy exists and is documented, the naalah_vedin and melekh_bedin rubric issue becomes a request to label the rubric as editorial rather than to remove it.
